test.name: Production-shaped tree: survey must surface Patrick's 1875 deed, which is attached to him as a person, not to any fact
test.description: ut_research_plan_bpx's scenario in the shape project_create writes today (#3066, #3140): every fact refs the blanket 'FamilySearch Family Tree' source S1, and Patrick's own attachment -- the 1875 Schuylkill County deed, S2 -- is referenced from persons[I2].sources, not from a fact. His Residence fact carries only the date and place; what he bought and where it is recorded is in S2 alone. Measures whether the survey reads a relative's person-level attachments, not only facts. No person carries an `ark`, so the profile-read step does not fire here (that is ut_research_plan_prof).

input.user_message: Create the first research plan for q_001 -- why did Michael Sheahan move to Schuylkill County around 1882?

judge_context: GENERAL RULE UNDER TEST: before planning new searches, the skill must survey what the project's tree already holds for every in-scope FAN-cluster person, not just the subject -- research-plan's own stated inputs include tree.gedcomx.json, which already holds this. Skipping straight to new-record planning without this survey is the specific failure this test guards against.

The tree gives Patrick Sheahan (I2, Michael's brother, linked via I3) an 1875 Residence fact in Schuylkill County, and attaches a source to Patrick himself (person-level, S2): 'Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, Recorder of Deeds, Deed Book 42, p. 118, Patrick Sheahan from James Kelly, 1875' -- a land purchase seven years before Michael's earliest confirmed Schuylkill presence (1882, log_002). The response should surface this: a sibling already established in the destination county years before Michael's own move bears directly on a 'why did Michael move' question (chain/pull migration via family already there).

This does not have to be a numbered plan item, but it must state what S2 records (a land purchase, a deed -- e.g. 'purchased land', 'Deed Book 42'), not just that Patrick lived in Schuylkill County in 1875: the fact gives only that much, and the place and year are already implicit in the question's framing. Content from S2 anywhere in the response -- survey section, plan item rationale, or summary -- counts; grade from what the response actually says. Total silence about Patrick, or naming only his residence and year, is the failure.

The plan should still include new record-type items for Michael's own movement and its cause (land/deed, tax, church/parish, probate, or naturalization, per the localities entry -- civil vital registration doesn't start until 1906, so it's out of scope for this 1870-1882 window) -- surfacing Patrick's fact is additive, not a replacement for planning new searches about Michael himself.

Should NOT plan a new search to (re)discover Patrick's 1875 land purchase -- the deed is already attached to him in the project's own tree (S2); planning a fresh search for it shows the skill re-searched rather than surveyed.

Grade on whether S2's content -- not just Patrick's existence, date or place -- reached the response, however briefly. Silence about Patrick is one failure; naming his 1875 residence without what the deed records is the same failure in a quieter form.
